clean_code.principle: Traceability accuracy (@req must name the requirement whose AC the code implements)
clean_code.description: The moved byteLimit carries `// @req IR-HTTP-013`, but IR-HTTP-013 (docs/spec/04.http-core.srs.md:4932) only declares bodyStream/bodyStream(long)/headerNames/rawHeaders/isFromTrustedProxy on the Request interface (AC-1 is about method declarations and generic return types); it says nothing about a 1..1073741824 range. The range of bodyStream(long) is FR-HTTP-031 AC-3 (04.http-core.srs.md:5155, AC-3 line 'bodyStream(0), (-1), (1073741825) throw IllegalArgumentException'; its implementation note names byteLimit() explicitly). The other three tags are justified: IR-JSON-002 AC-2 (jsonLimit range + message naming jsonLimit and 1..1073741824), IR-MULTIPART-001 AC-4 (formLimit 1..1073741824, IAE naming the setting), IR-APP-009 AC-3 (rawBodyLimit 0/-1/1073741825 rejected). The original private DefaultRestApp.byteLimit at HEAD had no @req tags at all, so these tags are new and the wrong one is introduced by this diff.
clean_code.suggested_fix: Replace `// @req IR-HTTP-013` with `// @req FR-HTTP-031` on LimitedInputStream.byteLimit (keep IR-JSON-002, IR-MULTIPART-001, IR-APP-009).

clean_code.principle: Acyclic dependencies / cohesion (helper should live with the constant it checks)
clean_code.description: The fix for CC-006 put the range check on LimitedInputStream rather than next to MAX_LIMIT on JsonBodyReader (which CC-006 suggested). JsonBodyReader already depends on LimitedInputStream (JsonBodyReader.java:40 `new LimitedInputStream(...)`); LimitedInputStream now depends back on JsonBodyReader.MAX_LIMIT in both the code and the javadoc {@link}, creating a source-level cycle between the two internal classes (the constant is inlined by javac, so not a runtime issue). It also puts an app-configuration argument validator ('<name> must be in 1..1073741824 bytes') on a stream class whose class doc and @req (FR-HTTP-020, FR-JSON-001) describe read-time overrun behaviour, and whose own constructor applies a different rule ('body limit must be positive'). Low priority; behaviour is unaffected.
clean_code.suggested_fix: Either move byteLimit to JsonBodyReader beside MAX_LIMIT (callers: DefaultRestApp x3, DefaultRequest.bodyStream(long)), or move MAX_LIMIT (the cross-body-limit bound) onto LimitedInputStream and have JsonBodyReader reference it, so the dependency runs one way.
